- Default both benchmark entry points to Python 3.14, with a dedicated `SCIENCE_RESEARCH_PYTHON` override. The PR research check previously inherited the gateway's Python 3.12, which could hide this failure. Product service environments keep their existing interpreters and dependencies.
- Require wheels in both entry points so missing wheels fail during resolution instead of starting native builds.
- Add a Biomni preparation regression that resolves the installed Hub API, supplies local download fixtures, verifies the pinned files and rejects corruption.

[NumPy 2.3.5](https://pypi.org/project/numpy/2.3.5/#files), [SciPy 1.16.3](https://pypi.org/project/scipy/1.16.3/#files) and [pandas 2.3.3](https://pypi.org/project/pandas/2.3.3/#files) publish CPython 3.14 Linux AMD64/ARM64 wheels. 520.author: zhaozhaozz
520.body:
On Windows, `serveStatic` compared a resolved path with a hard-coded `/` prefix. `path.resolve` returns backslashes there, so every SPA file and route failed the check and returned `400 Invalid path` before the file was read. The containment check now uses `path.relative` and rejects only a result of `..`, a leading `..` segment in the platform separator, or a result that is still absolute (including another drive or a UNC path).

## Path containment

`services/api/src/http/static.ts` keeps the existing status and body for a rejected path (`400`, `{"error":"Invalid path"}`). MIME types, reading a file inside the static root, falling back to `index.html`, and the built-in page when that file is missing are unchanged. A directory whose name is `..data` stays inside the root and is served. The check does not call `realpath`, so a symlink inside the root is still judged by its lexical path, as before.

## Validation

Focused unit test, from `services/api`:

```sh
node --import tsx --test src/http/static.test.ts
```

Result: tests 8, pass 8, fail 0, skipped 0. Four cases run on the host path implementation and the same four run with Node's `win32` path implementation (`resolve`, `relative`, `isAbsolute`, `extname`, and `sep`). The Windows cases use a backslash static root and map filesystem reads onto real fixture files. They were not run on a Windows machine.

Covered directly:

- `GET /` and `GET /assets/app.js` return 200 with the fixture body under win32 separators.
- `GET /../escape.txt` and `GET /%2e%2e/escape.txt` return 400 with the existing error body, and the file is not read. The same file also rejects the static root's parent, a same-prefix sibling directory, an encoded absolute path, an encoded backslash, another drive, and a UNC path.
- `GET /..data/keep.txt` returns 200. Missing routes still fall back to `index.html`, and a missing index still returns the built-in page.

Full local UT, ST, and E2E were not run. `git diff --check` on the commit is clean. The diff is these two files only.

## E2E user journeys

Not run. The user-visible failure happens when the static root uses Windows separators. On Linux the previous prefix check already returned 200 for files inside the root and 400 for escapes, so a browser, API, or CLI journey on this host cannot show the defect or the fix. No product stack was started. Real Windows and macOS were not used; the win32 half of the unit test is the evidence for that separator.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: on Windows, the browser UI and other static files load instead of every path returning 400. Rejected paths still return 400 Invalid path.

Compatibility and migration: none.

Fixes #481

520.title: fix(api): serve SPA static files on Windows instead of returning 400

`Rail` is the new left edge: 任务 and 设置, with the active one marked. It takes
the settings click as a callback rather than owning that state, because the
dialog belongs to `App`.

`Sidebar` is rewritten to the handoff's 科研任务 column: 新建任务, a search field,

The footer now reads plus, model pill, send. The plus opens the file picker and
states the per-file ceiling and the archive reason in its tooltip; uploading

528.author: ink999107
528.body:
The single-PR skill covers one change end to end, but this project proposes
larger changes as a stack of layers, and the rules that make a stack work were
spread across the session that built one. This adds them as a skill so the next
stack starts from the same procedure.

**Independent of the other pull requests in this batch.**

## What the skill covers

- The shape: one branch per layer cut from the layer below, one capability per
  layer, and no layer referencing a symbol that only exists above it.
- The body's stack section, so a reviewer knows which diff to read and in what
  order the pull requests merge.
- Rebase-merge rather than squash, because a squash collapses two layers into
  one commit and the next branch loses the parent it was built on.
- The push-through-the-Git-Data-API path for when `github.com` is unreachable
  for git transport, including the check that every server-side blob, tree and
  commit SHA matches the local one.
- What to do after a lower layer merges: reconstruct the rewritten commit,
  rebase the next layer onto it, verify the diff is still the layer's own, and
  push again.
- Review threads on lower layers: out of scope for the upper pull request, and
  answered rather than quietly resolved.

Allow once approves only the current request and does not save a grant. 540.author: zhaozhaozz
540.body:
Long agent runs were spending more and more time on the synchronous trajectory publish that happens before the next model request. `RefStore.commit` revalidated the whole reachable CAS closure on every publication, so the cost grew with history. The metadata cache already on main still walked that whole graph and treated device, inode, size, mtime and ctime as proof that bytes had not changed. This replaces that shortcut: a commit hashes only objects the current `VersionStore` has not admitted, and a full hash audit stays available everywhere it already was.

Fixes #230.

## Commit validation

`validateClosureForCommit` rehashes an object only when this `VersionStore` instance has not admitted it, and it stops at an admitted object instead of walking older history. An object is admitted only after a successful commit validation or a full audit has verified its bytes and, for a record, its whole dependency closure. Admission is published only when that whole closure passes. Bytes first admitted as a plain blob are still parsed when a later reference names them as a record. If the instance sees a failed read of an admitted object, it drops every admission, and a validation already in flight does not admit its result.

`validateClosure` is unchanged in role: it still rehashes every reachable object. `read`, `readRecord` and export reads still rehash on every call. A new `VersionStore` starts with nothing admitted, so the first commit of each Agent run still verifies the history it inherited. Record bytes, refs and history rows are unchanged, so export, provenance, recovery and debugging keep the same records.

Trust boundary, also written in `docs/en/developer-docs/cas.md` and `docs/zh/developer-docs/cas.md`: admission assumes CAS objects are append-only and that nothing outside this store changes an object after this process has verified it. File metadata is not evidence. An out-of-band rewrite or deletion is not noticed by a later commit in the same instance. It is noticed by every read and export, by `validateClosure`, and by the first commit of a new instance. There is no persistent admission index, so the saving does not survive a process restart. The in-memory table grows with the instance; each entry is one object key and a boolean. Workspace snapshot reuse still compares file identity and is outside this change.

`validateClosureForCommit` now returns how many objects it hashed, not the size of the closure. `validateClosure` still returns the number of reachable objects. In-repository callers ignore the commit helper's return value.

## Validation

Targeted tests on `daa749c6daceb24baf3c1b39d8443da34f5d9570`. On this host `node --test` prints the TAP summary and then the process is aborted (exit 134). The same abort happens for these suites after a clean summary. No assertion failed. Counts below are the TAP summaries.

| Command | TAP summary |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter "@sciencediscovery/cas..." build`, then `node --import tsx --test src/*.test.ts` in `packages/cas` | 33 tests, 33 pass, 0 fail |
| `node --import tsx --test src/*.test.ts` in `packages/trajectory` | 32 tests, 32 pass, 0 fail |
| `node --import tsx --test src/native-agent/versioning.test.ts src/agent-run/versioning-authorities.test.ts src/store-deletion.test.ts` in `services/api` | 14 tests, 14 pass, 0 fail |
| `node --import tsx --test src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` in `services/api` | 103 tests, 103 pass, 0 fail |

`per-turn commit validation does not grow with the trajectory` runs 40 turns and requires every turn to rehash exactly 5 objects (the new content, observation, state, context and step). A separate full audit of the final head hashes `5 * 40` objects. The new cases fail on the previous metadata-cache implementation, so they catch a return to walking history on the commit path.

A synthetic benchmark of this patch, not committed, timed only `RefStore.commit` (including the SQLite full sync). Each turn published a 64 KiB tool output, a 1 MiB workspace file, a state and a tree that grow with history, and a 32 KiB model input.

| Implementation | Turns | Step commit median, early to late | Context commit median, early to late | Total commit time |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| Full audit, before the metadata cache | 70 | 63.8 ms to 329.8 ms | 59.8 ms to 193.8 ms | 23.7 s |
| Metadata cache on main | 70 | 9.5 ms to 41.6 ms | 11.4 ms to 17.8 ms | 2.66 s |
| This patch | 70 | 3.7 ms to 3.7 ms | 9.7 ms to 11.8 ms | 1.02 s |
| Metadata cache on main | 200 | 9.7 ms to 183.6 ms | 12.0 ms to 50.7 ms | 41.6 s |
| This patch | 200 | 3.7 ms to 3.8 ms | 11.9 ms to 19.9 ms | 5.18 s |

At 200 turns the context commit still rises a little because the newly published state and tree themselves grow. The number of objects rehashed per turn stays constant; that is what the 40-turn test locks in. Full UT, ST and mocked E2E were not run locally.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED. Tested SHA: `daa749c6daceb24baf3c1b39d8443da34f5d9570`. No browser, HTTP API, CLI or local-stack user journey was executed.

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A long agent run keeps publishing trajectory records before the next model request | Per-turn commit checks stay with the newly published objects, and the recorded bytes stay exportable | Not run as a product journey. The CAS test above locks the rehash count at 5 per turn for 40 turns, and the API versioning and JiuwenSwarm agent tests still commit and read the same record shapes (14 pass, 103 pass). |
| Export or recovery reads a committed trajectory | A read rehashes and rejects replaced or missing bytes | Not run as a product journey. CAS tests reject a deleted object and a same-path byte replacement on read, on `validateClosure`, and on the first commit of a new store. |

This is a coverage gap, not a passing journey. GitHub Actions on this ready pull request is the full UT, ST and mocked E2E run.

## Release

User impact: long runs spend less time in synchronous trajectory publication before the next model request. Record format is unchanged. Within one process, a later commit does not notice an out-of-band rewrite of an object this process already verified; a read, an export, `validateClosure`, or the next process's first commit does.

542.author: zhaozhaozz
542.body:
An accepted remote Shell Execution became `unknown` / `unconfirmed` after repeated status-query failures or an API restart, and nothing asked the Runner about that same Execution ID again. A lost observation was easy to read as a finished job. Inspecting the execution now reconciles that record with the Runner and does not resubmit the command.

Related to #185. This does not close #185: the Agent → skill → NPU artifact check in that issue was not run.

## Reconciliation

`execution_status` on an `unknown` / `unconfirmed` record queries the Runner for the original Execution ID.

- A committed terminal record, or a recorded failure, is adopted and marked `committed`.
- A record that is still queued or running is followed again with the existing bounded retry. The stale unknown notice is withdrawn so the real end can notify the Agent again.
- An unreachable Runner, an unrecognized ID, a Runner-side unknown, or an end without a committed version stays `unknown` / `unconfirmed`. It is not reported as success or as a job failure.

Concurrent inspections of the same ID share one Runner query. Reconciliation never starts a second Shell Execution.

## Logs

Observation failures, recoveries, give-ups, restart orphans, and reconciliations log the Execution ID, Runner ID, consecutive failure count, underlying error message, cause, code, HTTP status, and Runner connection state (`ready`, `connecting`, `disconnected`, `failed`, or `local`).

## Known limits

- Provenance execution runs still store a lost observation as `status: "failed"` with `exitCode` null. That row is append-only, so a later reconciliation does not update it. Skill distillation and the memory graph read that row. Tracked in #541.
- Reconciliation runs when the execution is inspected (`execution_status`, including a foreground wait). There is no background sweep. The unknown notice tells the Agent to inspect it.
- Five immediate status failures still cross the existing threshold in a few seconds. A slower reconnect can show `unknown` first and then recover on the next inspection.
- For an explicit-handoff run, a reconciled result keeps the Runner's `createdFiles` / `modifiedFiles`. The normal completion path clears those lists. The shell record does not store the handoff flag.

## Validation

Fault injection uses a local HTTP Runner that accepts the job and then drops the status socket. No NPU.

- `node --import tsx --test services/api/src/shell-executions.test.ts services/api/src/agent-notifications.test.ts services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.test.ts`: tests 103, pass 103, fail 0, skipped 0.
- `node --import tsx --test services/api/src/shell-executions.test.ts`: tests 18, pass 18, fail 0, skipped 0.
- `node --import tsx --test packages/workspace/src/workspace.test.ts`: tests 56, pass 56, fail 0, skipped 0.

`pnpm ci:st` and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. The changed behavior is how the API treats a dropped Runner status connection, which the fault-injection unit tests cover.

## E2E user journeys

BLOCKED. Tested SHA: `b487d7ca5d94241ef0ee771695c5f8a1b1b16524`.

The user-visible path is an Agent inspecting an execution after a transient Runner status failure. No browser, API, CLI, or local-stack journey was executed. No NPU environment was available for the Agent → skill → NPU artifact flow named in #185. The unit tests above cover the status-loss path: one dropped status read recovers on the same Execution ID; five consecutive drops stay `unknown` / `unconfirmed`; a later inspection adopts the Runner's committed result without a second submission.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: After a remote command has been accepted, inspecting an unconfirmed execution asks the Runner about the same Execution ID and does not run the command again. Until that inspection, the record stays unknown rather than success or failure.

Compatibility and migration: none.

`ScienceDiscovery run` can pin thinking for the model a script uses, and the Reviewer and Idea Tree can think at their own effort. Interactive conversations already had this control. A batch run could not set it, and every delegated role followed one shared setting.

Fixes #47

## CLI

`run --thinking <off|auto|on>` and `run --effort <level>` set the session the run uses, the same way `--model` does. `--effort` turns thinking on. The accepted values are exactly the choices the composer offers for that model, read from `GET /api/sessions/:id/thinking-controls` after `--model` is applied.

A value the model does not accept exits 1 and names the accepted levels. It is not narrowed and it is not ignored. In JSONL mode the failure is one `error` line with `"code": "THINKING_NOT_ACCEPTED"`. `--effort` together with `--thinking off` or `--thinking auto` is rejected as a contradiction. Either flag on a model with no thinking control is rejected. With neither flag, the command does not read or write thinking settings.

The thinking fields themselves are written only after that check passes. Creating the project or session, and saving `--model`, can already have happened. A rejected flag does not start the run. That order matches other `run` setup.

`run --help` and the CLI reference (English and Chinese) document both options.

## Per-role effort

These are settings, not extra `run` flags.

- Reviewer: `reviewThinkingEffort`, resolved Global, then Project, then Session. It applies to Deep review on the session's task model. Unset, Deep review keeps the model profile's own thinking, which is what it used before this setting existed.
- Idea Tree: `roleThinkingEfforts` on the Idea Tree settings, keyed by stage (`ideate`, `design`, `assess`, `aggregate`, `propagate`). `assess` covers every assessor. A research freezes the map when it is created. The evolve model proxy narrows a requested stop to one the model accepts. A model with no effort control keeps its profile thinking. Unset, each stage is unchanged.

There is no new settings control in the Web or desktop UI. The same API surface already used for other Idea Tree settings carries these fields. Runtime behavior and the REST reference describe them.

The main run already stored `settingsSnapshot.thinkingMode` and `settingsSnapshot.thinkingEffort`. A CLI choice is written there. An Idea Tree research snapshot includes the configured map. Reviewer records had no effort field, and this change does not add one.

The composer and the API share one definition of which thinking choices a model accepts (`packages/schema`).

## Release

Resolved runtime settings gain a `reviewThinkingEffort` source of `unset` when it is not set. There is no new screen control.

544.body:
A terminal user can start an evolve search or an Idea Tree research and then only see an id. Progress and stop live on the Web cards. `evolve` and `idea` call the HTTP routes those cards already use, and they read the bearer token from the same data directory as `run`.

Fixes #50

## Commands

```text
ScienceDiscovery evolve list [--session <id>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id> [--after <sequence>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

`evolve stop` posts `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`, the dashboard Stop route. `idea stop` posts `operation: "end"`, the card's End research route. Pause and continue are only on Idea Tree, because an evolve search has no pause. `evolve list` stays global; `--session` only forwards the route's existing `sessionId` filter. There is no `run --wait`. A long run is followed with `watch`.

Output matches `run`: readable text on a terminal, and one JSON object per line when stdout is a pipe, so `jq` works. `watch` adds `reconnect` lines and a final `result` line. A failure is an `error` line.

`watch` replays, then follows live, and returns when the engine stops running. A dropped connection reconnects for about three minutes. Evolve continues after the last printed event sequence, so an event is not repeated. An Idea Tree frame is a full snapshot with no sequence, so a reconnect shows the current state and skips a frame already shown. `--after <sequence>` continues an evolve watch in a new process.

Ctrl-C stops watching and exits 130. It does not stop the engine. `stop` does that. This is different from `run`, where Ctrl-C cancels the turn `run` started.

Exit status follows `run` (0 completed, 1 failed, 130 cancelled):

| Exit status | evolve | idea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `succeeded` | `completed` |
| 130 | `stopped` | `ended` or `paused` |
| 1 | `failed` or `budget_exhausted` | `interrupted` |

A paused Idea Tree research exits 130 whether a person paused it or the token budget paused it. The engine records both as `paused`. `watch` also exits 1 when the run is missing, the token is refused, or the stream cannot be recovered.

## Validation

On `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e` (parent `9c33627b5ffc3c3ef397c114e267de6e6cc6dd10`, clean worktree):

- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — exit 0
- `cd services/launcher && pnpm test` — 188 pass, 0 fail (includes the CLI journey below)
- `node test/api/engine-cli-journey.mjs` — `outcome` PASS, repeated 5 times on this commit
- L1: architecture boundaries OK; CI test catalog OK; `docs:check` 0 issues; e2e metadata 0 errors (11 pre-existing legacy warnings)

## E2E user journeys

PASS on `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e`. Surface: CLI against the API process. Not a browser journey.

Command: `node test/api/engine-cli-journey.mjs`

The built CLI reads the token from the data directory. The journey uses a local fake model server and the evolve sidecar venv.

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recorded evolve search: list, get, candidate source, watch, `--after`, stop, missing id | Piped output is JSON. Watch of a finished success exits 0. Resume does not replay earlier events. Stop of an already finished success stays `succeeded`. A missing id exits 1. | PASS. Watch printed 6 events and exited 0. `--after 4` printed 2 events. |
| Live evolve watch, dropped connection, then CLI stop | Event sequences stay contiguous with no repeat. Stop uses the dashboard route. The run becomes `stopped` and watch exits 130. | PASS |
| Idea Tree watch, then pause | Watch follows the running research and exits 130 once it is paused. | PASS |
| Continue that research, then stop | Stop sends the card's end operation. The research ends. | PASS |
| A second research runs to completion | Watch exits 0. | PASS |

The live evolve step mounts the real evolve route handlers and orchestrator inside the API process. The public HTTP API has no route that creates a search, and API startup marks an unfinished search failed, so that step is not a separately started product process. Its sidecar is a stub. The same SSE routes forwarded through the default JiuwenSwarm adapter were not run. The CLI calls the same paths the Web cards call.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: from a terminal, evolve searches and Idea Tree researches can be listed, inspected, watched, and stopped. Idea Tree research can also be paused and continued. The commands, options, and exit statuses are in `help` and in the English and Chinese CLI reference.

Compatibility and migration: none. Existing `run` behavior is unchanged.

545.body:
Unchecking Web access for a Session still let the default JiuwenSwarm executor search the public web. Run assembly already left `web_search` and `web_fetch` out, but with JiuwenSwarm's own tools in use those two are dropped in favour of `free_search`, `paid_search` and `fetch_webpage`, and the adapter was never told to hide them. A search prompt still ran `free_search`.

Each JiuwenSwarm web tool now stands in only for the ScienceDiscovery tool the run actually has. When Web access is unchecked, `free_search`, `paid_search` and `fetch_webpage` are added to `hiddenJiuwenSwarmTools`. A later model call is renamed to an unavailable tool and returns "Ability not found". It does not run, and it does not raise a permission card. A tool policy and the native loop already gated `web_search` and `web_fetch` on the `web` connector id; this makes the JiuwenSwarm executor follow the same switch.

Session, Project and global runtime settings list connectors in the same three groups as the composer picker: Data sources, Web access and Custom MCP. Each entry uses the same name as the picker. Inherit and override are unchanged: the connector list is still one whole-list replacement.

The runtime reference describes those three kinds of entry, and the two switches a custom MCP server needs: the Session checkbox, and **Enable this MCP server** in System settings.

The default already on main is unchanged. A new data directory enables only `web`, and a custom MCP server stays off for the Session until it is checked. Issue #66 left the Web default open; `2a54d4ed` on main already chose "on, and can be turned off". This change does not pick a different default.

## Web access on JiuwenSwarm

`JIUWENSWARM_NATIVE_WEB_TOOLS` maps `web_search` to `free_search` and `paid_search`, and `web_fetch` to `fetch_webpage`. While JiuwenSwarm tools are in use, each of those names is hidden when the ScienceDiscovery tool it replaces is absent from the run, and kept when that tool is present. Our own `web_search` and `web_fetch` are still removed in that mode, so the model sees the stand-in rather than both.

## Settings groups

The composer picker and the settings editor share `groupConnectors`. An override still replaces the whole `enabledConnectorIds` list, including `web` and `custom-…` ids. Built-in data-connector checkboxes are the same control as before.

## Validation

Checked on `f1b82f13`, then rebased onto `b3a4911e`. `git range-diff` reports the patch unchanged (`f1b82f13` = `599b77ec`). The 13 commits on main since the previous base do not touch these files.

- `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm architecture:check`, `pnpm docs:links`: exit 0. Architecture check: 290 package source files. Docs links: 144 Markdown files.
- `apps/web` unit tests: 1013 pass, 0 fail.
- `packages/mcp` tests: 1 pass.
- `services/api` `jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`: 104 pass, 0 fail.
- API case that follows Web access from global, through a Project override that drops it, to a Session override that restores it: 1 pass.
- Broader API directories (`agent-run`, `native-agent`, `mcp`, `store.test.ts`, `server.test.ts`): 579 tests, 577 pass, 2 fail. Both failures also fail with `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` restored to the main version. One is PDF upload, because this host has no `services/paper` virtualenv. The other is `always-allow executes subagent code without permission requests or grants` (`status:unreviewed`): the stream records an extra `running` tool step.
- Mocked browser E2E on the JiuwenSwarm backend, the new session-capability journey plus the two `journey-custom-mcp` specs: 3 passed (1.0m).
- `journey-deepseek-web-settings` and `journey-plugin-composition`: 2 passed (29.8s).
- The new journey on the legacy backend: 1 passed (10.4s).
- The same new journey after restoring the pre-fix `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`: 1 failed, at the Web-off step. The model was still offered `free_search` and `fetch_webpage`, and `free_search` returned DuckDuckGo results. That is the bug this change closes.

Full `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st` and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run locally. GitHub Actions runs those layers on this pull request.

## E2E user journeys

PASS on `f1b82f13`. The rebased head has the same patch. Mocked browser, isolated local stack, scripted model. Formal runs did not use port 4310.

Scenario: a Session's capability checkboxes turn custom MCP and Web access on and off for the Agent.

- Open the picker. Expected: Data sources, Web access and Custom MCP are separate groups, and the server is listed by name. Actual: pass.
- Call the checked custom MCP. Expected: the Agent is offered that server's tool and the call succeeds. Actual: pass (`echo` succeeded).
- Uncheck Web access and the custom MCP, with permission mode set to ask. Expected: neither capability is offered, and a search prompt does not raise a permission card. Actual: pass. JiuwenSwarm offered no web tools; the attempt returned `Ability not found in resource_mgr: unavailable__free_search`. The legacy backend offered no web tools; the attempt returned `Unknown tool: web_search`. Permission decisions: 0. The reply contained no URL.
- Check both again while the server is disabled in System settings. Expected: Web access returns, and the server's tools stay absent. Actual: pass. The picker showed the server as unavailable.
- Open the same override in Session settings. Expected: the same three groups, with Web access and the server checked. Actual: pass.

The reverted-fix control failed that third step, as cited above.

Not covered: JiuwenSwarm's non-default `subagents=jiuwenswarm` mode. The system prompt still mentions web-search rules when Web access is off; a model may try the tool, and the call fails as a missing tool instead of running. An old configuration that disables the MCP plugin entirely still hides the whole picker, which is existing behaviour on main.

## Release

Release category: release:fix

User impact: unchecking Web access also removes JiuwenSwarm's own search and fetch tools. Settings editors group Data sources, Web access and Custom MCP the same way the composer picker does.

Compatibility and migration: none in this change. A Project or Session that saved an explicit connector list before `web` existed still does not include `web`. That behaviour is already on main.
